sections.h2: Where deeds are recorded in Bedford County
sections.html:
Land documents of every kind, from deeds and mortgages to leases, surveys, financing statements and rights of way, are filed with the Recorder of Deeds side of the combined Register and Recorder office. It occupies Room 106 on the first floor of the Bedford County Courthouse at 200 S Juliana St, Bedford, PA 15522. The phone is (814) 623-4836 and the email is randr@bedfordcountypa.org.

The files reach back to 1771, the year the county was created. Seven public workstations are available for title searchers, lenders and genealogists to browse on their own; employees will not do the searching for you.

Closing agents can e-file through Simplifile and CSC, which is why most sellers never see the counter. FraudSleuth, a free office service, lets owners check that every recording against their property was authorized.

Weekday counter hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with closures on designated county holidays. For recording, though, the window is 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and the same-day cutoff is 4:00 p.m.

The early cutoff catches people out. If the closing is tight, have the title company submit the deed long before 4:00 p.m. instead of hand-carrying paper in late in the day.

  • Mail goes to Recorder of Deeds Division, Bedford County Courthouse, 200 S Juliana St, Room 106, Bedford, PA 15522.
  • Every mailed filing needs a self-addressed stamped envelope for return of the documents.

The fee bill effective November 20, 2025 sets a deed at $59.75. State and county taxes the schedule folds in are part of that number, which is calculated for a document of up to four names and four pages. Past that, add $0.50 per name and $2.00 per page.

Deed$59.75

Pay the exact amount. Refunds are not possible. An overage of $5.00 or less stays with the office, and a bigger one sends the document back. A single check may cover no more than five documents.

Two layers of tax apply, each at 1% of the consideration, one state and one local, and both are due as the deed is recorded. Together that is 2%, on top of the recording fee. Payment may be by check, money order, cash, or credit or debit card. Make checks out to the Register Recorder as named on the fee bill.

A single check can cover both the tax and the recording fee. Land that lies in several municipalities or school districts needs a statement on the deed, in whole numbers, of how the local tax divides among them.

  • Deeds must show the true consideration or carry a completed Statement of Value.
  • Deeds, mortgages and assignments all need a signed Certificate of Residence.
  • The county web page links a Common Level Ratio sheet and the realty transfer tax forms.

The county seat is Bedford, in ridge and valley country. The 2025 population estimate of 47,480 is close to the 2020 figure of 47,567. There are 23,836 housing units and 19,750 households. Owners occupy 77.5% of homes, valued at a median of $179,000, while median gross rent is $784. New construction is scarce, so most buyers shop existing houses.

Beyond deeds and mortgages, the fee bill lists many real estate and miscellaneous instruments. Most affidavits, agreements, covenants, declarations, notices, restrictions and orders are $18.50. Amendments, cancellations, modifications, subordinations and terminations run $20.50, and leases of 30 years or longer, installment sales agreements, memorandums and oil and gas leases are $59.75.

Maps and plans are priced separately. A plat under 24 inches is $9.00 and one over 24 inches is $13.00. State highway and mining plans are $16.50 for the first page, with additional pages at $3.00. UCC financing statements and their ancillary filings are $100.00 each.

  • Notary public bond and commission: $39.50, which includes the commission tax and writ tax.
  • Notary name change or address change: $18.50.
  • Clean and Green filing: $18.50.
  • Partial release: $61.75.

For a home seller the practical lines are the deed, the mortgage satisfaction and any easement. If a title search turns up an old right of way or an unreleased mortgage, those are the instruments your closing agent will ask the office to record or clear.

sections.h2: Checklist before the deed goes in
sections.html:
Begin with the items that get a deed rejected when absent. Every deed, mortgage and assignment needs a Certificate of Residence completed and signed, and the deed must state the true consideration or come with a fully completed Statement of Value. Fees must be exact, so confirm the number with the office or your closing agent instead of rounding up.

Then decide who supplies the 2% tax and the recording fee, whether a title company runs the closing or you do it privately. Payment comes first; a deed cannot be recorded now and paid for later.

  • Confirm the grantee name and mailing address spelling.
  • Ask which municipality and school district the parcel falls in.
  • Call (814) 623-4836 with questions about the fee bill.
  • Keep a recorded copy for your records after closing.

sections.h2: If the title search finds a problem
sections.html: Old paperwork sometimes surfaces during a sale: a mortgage that was paid off but never released, or a right of way nobody remembers. Neither one has to stop the closing. Your title agent will ask the recorder to file the missing release or to record the easement properly, and the fee comes out of the settlement figures. The sooner you hand over your own copies of old deeds and payoff letters, the faster these loose ends get tied up. Do not assume the buyer will overlook them, because a lender or inspector often will not.

sections.h2: Getting a copy of a recorded document
sections.html:
Records can be viewed online through the Recorder of Deeds Records Online link on the county page, or at the public workstations in Room 106. Photocopies are $0.25 a page at the counter, pages larger than 11 by 17 inches are $2.00, and a certified copy is $1.00 plus $0.25 for each page.

The office does not take part in title searches and cannot offer legal advice, so ask an attorney what a document means. Originals go back to whoever presented them, unless the filer directs otherwise, and mailed documents must come with a postage-paid return envelope. Military discharge papers are confidential and available only to the service member or a service organization. Recording a DD-214 and any certified copies are free.

sections.h2: How a cash sale fits the recording process
sections.html: A cash buyer still needs the deed recorded, taxed at 2% and filed with a Certificate of Residence. What changes is that no lender is waiting on paperwork, so the title company can often send the deed in as soon as signatures are done. If you still have a mortgage, make sure a satisfaction piece is recorded after payoff, at the fee shown above, so the record shows the loan as paid.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee for a deed in Bedford County?
faqs.a: It is $59.75 for a deed with up to four names and four pages, under the fee bill effective November 20, 2025. Each added name is $0.50 and each added page is $2.00.

faqs.q: Is the transfer tax included in the Bedford County deed fee?
faqs.a: The fee bill says its listed fees include state and county taxes. The realty transfer tax itself is 1% state and 1% local of the consideration, collected at recording, so ask the office how your deed's total is calculated.

faqs.q: Can I record a Bedford County deed electronically?
faqs.a: Yes. The office accepts e-recording through Simplifile and CSC, along with mail and in-person filing. Most sellers leave this to the title company.

faqs.q: When does same-day recording stop in Bedford County?
faqs.a: Same-day recording stops at 4:00 p.m. even though the office stays open until 4:30 p.m. Call (814) 623-4836 if a closing is running late.

faqs.q: Does the Bedford County office return my original deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Originals go back to the person who presented them unless the office is told otherwise, and mailed documents need a postage-paid return envelope.
